description:
Cauley Ferrari is proud to offer this stunning Ferrari 328 GTS finished in rare Prugna Metallic exterior over a Crema leather interior. The final iteration of a 15-year-old design was produced from 1986 to 1989. This classic Pininfarina-designed car has aged gracefully, while the performance is still engaging today. The 328 produces 270hp and weighs just under 2,800lbs. The newly restyled Ferrari 328 was released in 1985 as a replacement for the aging 308, which had at that point been in production for nearly 10 years. The 328 was offered from the start as both a fixed-roof coupe (GTB) and as a Targa (GTS). Ferrari 328 production would last a total of four years, from 1985 to 1989, when it was replaced by the all-new 348. A total of 7,412 cars rolled off the assembly line at Maranello, with 6,068 GTS versions being produced alongside 1,344 GTB models.

The 328 is considered one of the most reliable classic Ferraris. An evolution of the 308, launched in 1975, its a relatively simple car, free from electronic wizardry. Bosch K-Jetronic mechanical fuel injection was the order of the day here. Unlike many Ferraris, a 328 can be serviced without removing the engine, which keeps servicing costs down.

The 1987 Porsche 911 Carrera Cabriolet represents one of the most desirable years of the legendary 3.2 Carrera, combining the unmistakable look and feel of the classic air-cooled 911 with the highly sought-after G50 5-speed manual transmission. Finished in timeless Black over a Tan leather interior and showing just 54,000 miles, this is a great opportunity to own an increasingly collectible air-cooled Porsche at an attractive price point.

This 911 remained with its previous owner for many years and was always garage kept. The body presents very well overall, especially considering its age, with only minor cosmetic flaws consistent with a properly enjoyed 39-year-old car. Black over Tan is about as classic as it gets on an air-cooled 911, and the Cabriolet body gives you the full open-air experience while retaining the iconic shape that made this generation of 911 famous.

Power comes from Porsche's legendary 3.2-liter air-cooled flat-six, paired with the desirable Getrag G50 5-speed manual transmission introduced on the Carrera for the 1987 model year. The G50's smoother shifting and hydraulic clutch make these later 3.2 Carreras particularly sought after by enthusiasts, while still delivering the mechanical, analog driving experience that makes an air-cooled 911 so special.

A brand-new convertible top was installed in 2025 and presents beautifully. The power top mechanism is currently not operational, however, so the top must presently be raised and lowered manually. We want to be completely transparent about this condition: the vehicle is being offered as-is and has been priced accordingly.

With only 54k miles, long-term previous ownership, a classic Black-over-Tan color combination, the desirable G50 5-speed, and a recently installed convertible top, this is an excellent entry point into air-cooled 911 ownership. It isn't being represented as a concours-perfect example, nor is it priced like one. Instead, it's an attractive, honest 3.2 Carrera Cabriolet that can be driven and enjoyed without being afraid to put miles on it.

Air-cooled 911s have become increasingly difficult to find at approachable price points, particularly G50-equipped cars with reasonable mileage. If you've been looking for a classic 911 that you can actually get out and enjoy, this one deserves a serious look.

2005 MERCEDES-BENZ SL65 AMG ROADSTER

VIN: WDBSK79F45F093918
47,507 MILES | SILVER OVER GRAY | 6.0L BI-TURBO V12 | AMG | HARDTOP CONVERTIBLE

Okay...

I had an entire introduction planned for this car.

Then I realized...

IT'S AN SL65 AMG.

If you know...

YOU'RE ALREADY LOOKING FOR YOUR KEYS.

And if you don't know?

Allow me about 30 seconds to ruin every other SL you've been shopping for.

6.0-LITER.BI-TURBO.V12.

That's it.

That's the ad.

We can all go home.

Actually, no.

Because Mercedes-Benz apparently decided a luxury convertible needed a hand-built twin-turbocharged V12 producing 604 horsepower and 738 lb-ft of torque.

IN 2005.

Read that again.

738 LB-FT.

In a two-seat Mercedes roadster.

Because apparently Germany was completely unsupervised in the early 2000s.

THIS IS NOT AN SL500.

Not an SL55.

Not an SL with AMG wheels.

SL65 AMG.

The big one.

The ridiculous one.

The one Mercedes built for the person who walked into the dealership and said:

What's the most unnecessary version?

THIS.AND THIS ONE HAS 47,507 MILES.

Not 147,000.

FORTY-SEVEN THOUSAND.

Silver.

Gray interior.

And the condition?

DEAD NEW.

You don't have to squint.

You don't have to use your imagination.

You don't have to listen to somebody explain that it's really clean for the year.

NO.

IT'S CLEAN.

Period.

THE LAST OWNER DIDN'T JUST OWN IT.THEY PAMPERED IT.

Service.

Care.

Condition.

Preservation.

This thing even came to us with its CAR COVER.

That's the kind of previous owner you want when you're buying a 20+ year-old V12 AMG.

Some people park their car.

THIS GUY TUCKED IT INTO BED.

Probably whispered goodnight to it.

And after seeing the condition?

WE'RE NOT EVEN MAKING FUN OF HIM.

We understand.

AND THEN YOU START LOOKING AROUND IT.

AMG bodywork.

AMG wheels.

Massive AMG brakes.

Quad exhaust.

Retractable hardtop.

Leather everywhere.

Wood trim.

Luxury everywhere you touch.

And underneath all that civilized Mercedes-Benz behavior...

TWO TURBOS ARE FORCE-FEEDING A V12.

This car has absolutely no idea what personality it wants.

Luxury roadster?

Grand tourer?

Autobahn missile?

Convertible?

YES.PUT THE TOP DOWN.

Now you're cruising.

Quiet.

Comfortable.

Classy.

Silver Mercedes.

Nothing to see here.

Then your right foot moves approximately three inches.

OH.THERE'S THE V12.

This is the kind of car where the passenger asks:

Why are we going this fast?

And the driver responds:

I BARELY TOUCHED IT.2005 WAS A DIFFERENT TIME.

Mercedes wasn't downsizing.

They weren't asking how many cylinders they could remove.

They weren't putting giant screens where the dashboard used to be.

They took their flagship roadster...

Stuffed a twin-turbo V12 into it...

Sent it to AMG...

And apparently nobody in accounting had the courage to stop them.

THANK GOD.HERE'S HOW THIS SALE IS PROBABLY GOING TO GO.

You see the ad.

You stare at the pictures.

You tell yourself you don't need another car.

You Google SL65 AMG V12.

Huge mistake.

Twenty minutes later you're calculating garage space.

An hour later you're explaining to somebody why a 2005 Mercedes is suddenly extremely important.

Then my phone rings.

SAVE US BOTH THE TIME.

Send me your Amex.

I'll get the paperwork ready.

SEE YOU SOON.THE MARUTI WAY

No recon fees.

No prep fees.

No games.

One $499 Doc Fee plus tax and DMV.

Because if you're buying a twin-turbo V12 AMG roadster, you've already got enough going on.

BOTTOM LINE

2005 Mercedes-Benz SL65 AMG Roadster

47,507 Miles

Silver over Gray

6.0L Bi-Turbo V12

604 Horsepower

738 LB-FT of Torque

AMG

Retractable Hardtop

Exceptionally Preserved

Pampered Previous Ownership

Well Serviced

Car Cover Included

THIS ONE DOESN'T NEED TO BE SOLD.IT JUST NEEDS TO BE SEEN.

Because somebody who understands exactly what SL65 AMG means is going to see those pictures.

They're going to see 47,507 miles.

They're going to see the condition.

They're going to see the service.

And they're not going to send us seventeen questions.

THEY'RE JUST GOING TO SHOW UP.

description: There are low-mileage collector cars, and then there are automobiles that essentially never entered service. This is one of those cars. Showing an astonishing 71 original miles, this one-owner 1998 Chevrolet Corvette Indianapolis 500 Pace Car Convertible has spent nearly its entire life preserved rather than driven. Nearly three decades later, it remains an extraordinary example of one of the most recognizable and unapologetically bold Pace Car Corvettes Chevrolet ever produced.For the 82nd running of the Indianapolis 500, Chevrolet selected the then-new C5 Corvette Convertible as the Official Pace Car. To commemorate the occasion, Chevrolet offered the special Z4Z Indianapolis 500 Pace Car Replica, finished in exclusive Pace Car Purple Metallic with vivid yellow Indianapolis 500 graphics, matching yellow wheels, a black convertible top and its unmistakable yellow-and-black leather interior. Final production totaled just 1,163 examples, including five pilot cars, making the 1998 Pace Car a special chapter in Corvette history. This particular example was purchased new by its one and only owner and today shows just 71 original miles. And it looks like it. The Pace Car Purple Metallic finish remains spectacular, with tremendous depth and shine, while the elaborate factory Indianapolis 500 graphics remain beautifully preserved. The distinctive yellow wheels are equally impressive and, combined with the purple finish and dramatic graphics, create one of the most unforgettable factory appearances ever offered on a Corvette. Subtle it wasn't in 1998, and nearly three decades later it certainly hasn't become any less memorable. The interior may be even more remarkable. The yellow-and-black leather sport seats, carpeting, dashboard, console, steering wheel, controls and switchgear show virtually none of the wear normally associated with a 28-year-old automobile. The contrasting yellow stitching on the steering wheel and shifter is another wonderful Pace Car detail. Simply put, the photographs show an interior that has essentially never experienced normal automobile use. Under the hood is Chevrolet's all-aluminum 5.7-liter LS1 V8 producing 345 horsepower, backed in this example by the electronically controlled four-speed automatic transmission. The engine compartment retains an exceptionally clean, original appearance and has not been cosmetically restored or dressed in an attempt to make an old Corvette look like a low-mile automobile. Because this Corvette spent so much of its life in long-term storage, we did not simply install a battery and offer it for sale. It was carefully recommissioned and serviced, including a new battery, replacement fuel pump and fuel injectors, fresh fuel and fluid service. The goal was to properly address the mechanical needs created by decades of extremely limited use while preserving the originality that makes this Corvette so special. It now starts, runs and operates beautifully. The underside tells the same story. The chassis, floors, aluminum suspension components, hardware and factory finishes retain an exceptionally clean and untouched appearance. Nothing has been freshly painted or cosmetically refinished underneath to create the illusion of preservation. At only 71 miles, it simply hasn't experienced the road use normally found underneath even the nicest surviving C5 Corvettes. Perhaps the ultimate evidence of that preservation remains at each corner. This Corvette is still riding on its original Goodyear Eagle F1 tires—the same tires it left Chevrolet with in 1998. We intentionally chose not to replace them because, on a Corvette with only 71 miles, they have become an important part of the automobile's history. After nearly three decades of storage, the tires have developed significant flat spotting and are considered preservation/display items rather than tires intended for regular road use. A future owner wishing to drive the car should replace them, but we felt the originals belonged on the automobile when it was offered for sale. Documentation is equally impressive. The original window sticker, showing a delivered price of $50,029, remains with the Corvette along with its original owner's materials and portfolio, Indianapolis 500 Pace Car literature, both sets of original keys and remotes, and additional original documentation accumulated by its one owner. On a collector automobile with mileage this extraordinary, those materials are an important part of its provenance. That's ultimately what separates this Corvette from simply being another beautiful 1998 Pace Car. There is no shortage of restored, detailed and low-mile collector Corvettes. What cannot be recreated is one-owner history, 71 original miles, original factory-installed tires, original documentation and nearly three decades of genuine preservation. It would be very easy to install new tires, begin driving it and turn this into another exceptionally nice 1998 Corvette Pace Car. There is no way to turn one back into a 71-mile example. For the Corvette collector searching for an extraordinary preservation automobile rather than simply another Pace Car replica, opportunities at this mileage level are exceedingly difficult to duplicate. One owner. 71 original miles. Original tires. Original documentation. Properly recommissioned after long-term preservation. It hasn't been restored to look like a 71-mile Corvette. It is a 71-mile Corvette. Long-Term Ownership

According to the previous owners, this Miata was purchased by them in 2003 and remained in their care for more than 20 years.

That kind of ownership history is becoming increasingly difficult to find with first-generation Miatas, many of which have passed through numerous owners, been heavily modified, or repurposed as track cars.

This example has instead remained much closer to its original character.

Documented Care

The car comes with a collection of receipts and service records documenting maintenance over the years.

In 2013, it received an original-style replacement tan convertible top with a zippered plastic rear window and pre-attached rain rail.

A Pioneer receiver and upgraded audio components were also professionally installed in 2013.

More recently, at 64,188 miles in November 2025, the car received documented cooling-system service including a radiator, thermostat, coolant, and radiator cap.

Since acquiring the car, we also addressed a minor oil seep by installing a new valve cover gasket.

Why This One Stands Out

A first-generation Miata doesn t need much explaining. Mazda got the formula right from the beginning: compact dimensions, low weight, naturally aspirated power, a manual transmission, and a chassis designed around driver engagement rather than outright speed.

What makes this particular example special is the combination of low mileage, C Package specification, attractive red/tan color combination, 5-speed manual, long-term previous ownership, and a largely stock presentation.

It hasn t been turned into something it was never meant to be. It still feels like an NA Miata should.

For someone looking for a clean, well-kept example of one of the most important Japanese sports cars of the modern era, this one deserves serious consideration.

description:
The 2021 Mazda MX-5 Miata RF Club turns an ordinary drive into something worth looking forward to, combining the compact proportions of an iconic two-seat sports car with the distinctive style of the RF design. The Club trim adds an enthusiast-focused personality to the experience, making this Miata an appealing choice for drivers who value connection, agility, and the simple enjoyment of getting behind the wheel.

The RF body style gives the Miata a particularly striking presence. Its sleek roofline creates a coupe-like silhouette while preserving the open-air character that makes the MX-5 experience so memorable. With its low stance, compact dimensions, and purposeful proportions, the Miata RF looks ready for a winding road even when it is sitting still. It is a sports car designed to make the journey feel every bit as important as the destination.

Behind the wheel, the MX-5 Miata's driver-centered philosophy takes priority. The intimate two-seat cabin places the focus on the road ahead, creating the kind of environment that makes a favorite back road, coastal drive, or quiet early-morning trip feel special. Rather than relying on size or excess, the Miata delivers its personality through a lightweight-feeling, compact sports-car format built around driver involvement.

The Club trim fits naturally with that enthusiast-oriented character. This is a Miata for shoppers who appreciate a vehicle that feels different from the typical commuter car or crossover. description: The 2000 Mazda MX-5 Miata is a lightweight, rear-wheel-drive sports car celebrated for its pure, engaging driving experience. Its two-seat convertible layout, low seating position, and short-throw shifter create an unmistakably sporty feel. With its timeless styling, modest running costs, and enormous enthusiast following, the 2000 MX-5 Miata remains an appealing choice for anyone seeking an affordable classic roadster. It is a car that rewards every mile with simplicity, balance, and fun.

This van also features an installed Adrian Steel cargo partition/bulkhead, helping separate the driver compartment from tools, equipment, and cargo.Engine & PerformanceThe Transit Connect is built for businesses that need cargo capability without stepping up to a full-size commercial van. Its 2.0L four-cylinder engine and 8-speed automatic provide an efficient, easy-to-drive combination, while the factory window sticker lists an EPA estimate of approximately 25 MPG combined, 24 city and 26 highway.Other useful equipment includes four-wheel disc brakes with ABS, Hill Start Assist, electronic power steering, AdvanceTrac with Roll Stability Control, and an engine block heater.Interior & TechnologyThe cabin is designed to remain practical during long workdays. It features Ebony cloth front bucket seats, power windows and locks, remote keyless entry, cruise control, steering-wheel-mounted audio controls, air conditioning, tilt/telescoping steering wheel, overhead storage, dual 12V powerpoints, and a Smart Charging USB port.The factory SYNC equipment adds Bluetooth connectivity and a rearview camera, while Pre-Collision Assist with Automatic Emergency Braking provides additional driver confidence.Cargo & Business UtilityThis LWB Transit Connect is especially well suited for contractors, electricians, HVAC technicians, plumbers, maintenance companies, delivery services, and mobile service businesses.The cargo area includes an Adrian Steel metal partition, durable black cargo flooring, cargo tie-down points, rear cargo lighting, dual sliding side doors, and 180-degree swing-out rear cargo doors. The partition helps keep the work area separated from the passenger compartment and provides an excellent starting point for additional shelving, bins, drawers, or tool organization.The original vehicle was also configured as an Adrian Steel ship-through unit, reinforcing its commercial-purpose setup.Condition & HistoryCARFAX reports 2 previous owners, with commercial and lease use. The vehicle was previously owned in North Carolina and has no accidents or damage reported.CARFAX also reports no structural damage, no airbag deployment, no indication of odometer rollback, and no branded title problems. The available history includes a pre-delivery inspection and later maintenance inspection.CARFAX currently lists a Ford manufacturer emissions recall involving Powertrain Control Module reprogramming. Customers can contact an authorized Ford dealer to verify current status and complete any applicable manufacturer remedy.With only 13,627 miles, a clean accident history, Long Wheelbase configuration, and Adrian Steel partition already installed, this Transit Connect is a strong option for a business looking for a clean, efficient work van.Remaining Ford Factory WarrantyBased on the current mileage of 13,627 and the provided Ford/CARFAX warranty estimate as of September 11, 2026, this Transit Connect is estimated to have factory coverage remaining.Estimated remaining coverage includes approximately 1 month or 22,373 miles of Basic Warranty, plus approximately 25 months or 46,373 miles of Powertrain coverage and Roadside Assistance. Corrosion coverage is estimated at approximately 25 months with unlimited mileage.Factory coverage is subject to Ford's original warranty terms, in-service date, exclusions, and final verification through an authorized Ford dealer.Powerhouse WarrantyIn addition to any remaining applicable factory coverage, this vehicle includes added peace of mind through Oswego Motors with our 3 Year / 100,000 Mile Powerhouse Limited Warranty. Coverage includes major internally lubricated engine components and towing reimbursement in the event of a covered breakdown.
